items.informal_name: Coefficient of Taylor Expansion at $ r $: $ \text{coeff}_n(f(X + r)) = D^{(n)}f(r) $
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (r : R) (f : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ),
  ((Polynomial.taylor r) f).coeff n = Polynomial.eval r ((Polynomial.hasseDeriv n) f)
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ f $ over a semiring $ R $, natural number $ n $, and element $ r \in R $, the coefficient of $ X^n $ in the Taylor expansion $ f(X + r) $ equals the evaluation of the $ n $-th Hasse derivative of $ f $ at $ r $. The Hasse derivative $ D^{(n)} $ scales monomials $ a_i X^i $ by $ \binom{i}{n} a_i X^{i - n} $.

items.informal_name: First Coefficient of Taylor Expansion Equals Derivative
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (r : R) (f : Polynomial R),
  ((Polynomial.taylor r) f).coeff 1 = Polynomial.eval r (Polynomial.derivative f)
items.informal_description: The coefficient of $ X $ in the Taylor expansion of a polynomial $ f $ at a point $ r $ in a semiring $ R $ is equal to the derivative of $ f $ evaluated at $ r $, i.e., $ \text{coeff}_1(\text{Taylor}_r(f)) = f'(r) $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient Formula for Hasse Derivative of Order k
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ),
  ((Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f).coeff n = ↑((n + k).choose k) * f.coeff (n + k)
items.informal_description: For any natural number $ n $, the coefficient of $ X^n $ in the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of a polynomial $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ is equal to $ \binom{n + k}{k} $ multiplied by the coefficient of $ X^{n + k} $ in $ f $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k Applied to a Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f = f.sum fun i r => (Polynomial.monomial (i - k)) (↑(i.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $ and a polynomial $ f \in R[X] $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ applied to $ f $ is given by $ D^{(k)}(f) = \sum_{i} \binom{i}{k} \cdot a_i \cdot X^{i - k} $, where $ a_i $ is the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ f $. This expression sums over all monomials in $ f $, scaling each by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{i}{k} $ and reducing the exponent by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Zeroth Coefficient of Taylor Expansion Equals Polynomial Evaluation at r
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (r : R) (f : Polynomial R), ((Polynomial.taylor r) f).coeff 0 = Polynomial.eval r f
items.informal_description: The constant term of the Taylor expansion of a polynomial $ f $ at $ r $, denoted as $ \text{coeff}_0(f(X + r)) $, is equal to the evaluation of $ f $ at $ r $, i.e., $ f(r) $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient of Natural Degree in Taylor Expansion Equals Leading Coefficient
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (r : R) (f : Polynomial R),
  ((Polynomial.taylor r) f).coeff f.natDegree = f.leadingCoeff
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ and an element $ r \in R $, the coefficient of the natural degree term in the Taylor expansion of $ f $ at $ r $ (i.e., the polynomial $ f(X + r) $) is equal to the leading coefficient of $ f $. This holds because the highest-degree term in $ f(X + r) $ retains the leading coefficient of $ f $ after binomial expansion.

items.informal_name: Taylor Expansion Evaluation Identity: $(\mathrm{taylor}\, r\, f)(s) = f(s + r)$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (r : R) (f : Polynomial R) (s : R),
  Polynomial.eval s ((Polynomial.taylor r) f) = Polynomial.eval (s + r) f
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ f \in R[X] $ and elements $ r, s \in R $, the evaluation of the Taylor expansion of $ f $ at $ r $ at $ s $ equals $ f(s + r) $.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (r : R) (i : ℕ) (k : R),
  (Polynomial.taylor r) ((Polynomial.monomial i) k) = Polynomial.C k * (Polynomial.X + Polynomial.C r) ^ i
items.informal_description: For any natural number $i$ and element $k$ in the semiring $R$, the Taylor series expansion at $r$ applied to the monomial polynomial $kX^i$ results in the polynomial $k(X + r)^i$.
